newsitem.title: USA: Seagram's MCA music arm's growth seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Seagram's MCA music arm's growth seen continuing.

text.p: New management and recent acquisitions have boosted sales of MCA Music Entertainment Group, which is expected to continue gaining market share through further acquisitions, sources said on Wednesday.

"Companies either grow market share (internally) or buy it. Those are the two ways to do it and MCA is focusing on both. By doing so, it is doubling its odds," said Recording Industry Association of America President Hilary Rosen.

Seagram Co. Ltd 's MCA Music, long viewed an industry laggard, is clawing its way through the ranks with some veterans it lured from Time Warner Inc.'s Warner Music and its acquisition of a 50 percent stake in Interscope Records, a label previously owned by Time Warner.

For the three months ended Sept. 30, MCA Music Entertainment's revenues rose only moderately to $345 million from $339 million, but the company said Tuesday its Uni distribution arm was having its strongest sales month in its history.
Also, for the first time, MCA topped the charts in current album market share for the week ended Nov. 10.
Interscope is dominating the pop charts with a string of hits from rock and rhythm and blues acts like Bush, No Doubt and Nine Inch Nails. It also distributes rap music by Death Row Records.

Additionally, industry sources cite persistent rumors MCA is seeking to buy music giant EMI Group Plc, which split from rentals company Thorn Plc three months ago. MCA declines to comment on speculation.
At the time of its split with Thorn, EMI was valued at about $9.74 billion.
On a smaller scale, sources this week also cited rumors that Interscope is in talks to buy American Recordings, a deal that would terminate that label's joint venture with Warner Bros.
One source close to the company said Interscope chief Jimmy Iovine has been in casual talks with Rick Rubin, who owns American Recordings, but knew no further details.

Industry sources attribute the turnaround at MCA Music, which is expected to report a record fourth quarter, to a restructuring implemented by Seagram Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. and MCA President Ron Meyer.
They recruited several executives from Warner Music, including Doug Morris, who was named chairman and chief executive a year ago.
"When I joined MCA last year, we dedicated ourselves to building the music company of the future," said Morris.
"I feel we have made significant strides forward in achieving that goal and we now have some of the most talented executives and artists within the MCA family," he said.
"Everybody there has a combination of commitment and talent and a desire to prove something and those three things are powerful combinations," Rosen of the RIAA said.
While many industry sources acknowledge MCA is emerging as a powerful player in the $12 billion music industry, they still say the company has a long way to go to prove itself.

"There's no doubt that Interscope and Death Row have helped MCA immensely. Its country music sector has always been strong, but it still lags in the modern and alternative rock field," one music attorney said.
"Its MCA Records and Universal Records have had some moderate successes, but they have yet to really break a major act," he said.
